title: spec review: S2b v2: capacity snapshot and fallback treat claude:<tier> rows as Claude capacity; README plug-and-play
spec:
Goal T-1334 (S1 T-1352 merged). Replaces T-1357 after spec review T-1359. Claude executor rows have id "claude:<tier>" (S2a contract), so running claude-row tasks carry executor "claude:<tier>" and are already counted by daemon.running_claude_workers (daemon.py:470, "claude:" prefix) into snapshot["claude_workers_free"]; no change there. The dispatch-time check (executor.start -> pool.pick) stays authoritative and holds "no account with headroom"; the snapshot rule below is advisory and read-only.

1. capacity.snapshot (capacity.py:9): each executor row carries "provider"; every reader uses row.get("provider", "codex") so rows built elsewhere (concurrency.py, speculation.py, tests) without the key stay codex.
2. One helper _usable(row, snapshot, free=None) used by eligible_executors_from_snapshot (:54), admit (:101) and the "fallback" flag (:45): codex row -> today's checks; claude row -> today's checks (enabled, role, band, cooling_s == 0, row free, day_tasks_left) plus at least one snapshot account with cooling_s == 0 plus the shared counter > 0. fallback = enabled execute rows exist and none is usable (with the shared counter at its snapshot value).
3. admit: free["claude_rows"] = snapshot["claude_workers_free"]; the `available` filter (capacity.py:127) requires free["claude_rows"] > 0 for claude rows; the imminent-reservation blocker (:141) treats a claude row as having min(row free, free["claude_rows"]); on choosing a claude row decrement both. The legacy "claude" pseudo-executor only appears when fallback is True, i.e. when no claude row is usable, so the two never draw in the same pass.
4. _reason (:75): a claude row otherwise eligible but shared counter 0 -> "account_capacity"; every account cooling -> "cooldown".
5. daemon._codex_available (daemon.py:454): a claude row counts when enabled, has "execute", is not cooling and at least one pool account is not cooling (same advisory rule; no Pool.pick, no window roll).
6. README.md "Executors and routing" (README.md:278): Claude rows (id "claude:<tier>", tier alias in [models], model optional and must match the alias, roles, band, max_parallel, daily_budget_tasks), headroom from [[claude_accounts]] and [limits].max_parallel_claude_workers, reviewer never runs the executing model, plug-and-play: add a [models] alias + a claude:<alias> row for a new Claude model, add a codex row for a new Codex model, enabled=false on every codex row to run without Codex.
Tests (unittest.TestCase methods): two ready tasks and one shared slot -> one admitted, one deferred account_capacity; every account cooling -> claude row not eligible, reason cooldown; all codex rows cooling + healthy claude row -> fallback False and the claude row eligible; codex-only snapshot rows without "provider" -> admit result equals hard-coded expected ids; a running task with executor "claude:opus" lowers claude_workers_free via running_claude_workers; _codex_available with a claude row, one account not cooling vs all cooling. No pool.toml edit, no new dependencies. Additive; git revert restores the old admission.

risks.issue: The spec defines fallback as 'no enabled execute row is usable', and _usable includes free, band and day_tasks_left. Today fallback means only 'all enabled rows cooling'. If every codex row is saturated but healthy, fallback flips True and tasks route to the legacy 'claude' pseudo-executor instead of waiting. daemon._fallback_mode (daemon.py:463) still keys on cooling only, so the two disagree, and the 'codex-only unchanged' criterion breaks.

free_slots (daemon.py:483-499) is not in the spec. It sums max_parallel minus running for every non-cooling execute row, claude rows included, with no shared claude cap and no account check. capacity_reason at daemon.py:773 also ignores claude rows. With scheduler mode off, admit is skipped and _first_come_order over-dispatches claude tasks, which executor.start/pool.pick then holds.

The advisory _codex_available rule (enabled, execute, not cooling, one account free) ignores band, daily budget and row saturation, which both the snapshot _usable and pool.eligible_executors apply. With every codex row cooling and a claude row that is over budget or out of band, _codex_available stays True, so fallback_claude never fires and tasks hold indefinitely.

choice_key (:132) and the imminent blocker (:141) read free[executor_id] (row free). The spec does not say whether they use the effective min(row free, claude_rows). A claude row with free=4 and shared counter 1 can outrank a codex row, and the `free==1` blocker check can misfire.

concurrency.py and speculation.py read snapshot rows and claude_workers_free but are outside scope. The spec does not check that select_limit does not double count the shared counter against per-row free for claude rows.

suggested_spec_changes: Keep the snapshot fallback flag cooling-based: all enabled execute rows cooling AND no claude row with a non-cooling account and counter > 0. Use _usable only in eligible_executors_from_snapshot and admit.

Add daemon.free_slots and the dispatch capacity_reason (daemon.py:773) to scope. Cap claude-row slots by claude_workers_free and gate them on a non-cooling account, or state explicitly that the mismatch is accepted.

Make _codex_available apply the same band, budget and saturation semantics as the snapshot rule, or document why it differs, so _fallback_mode and snapshot['fallback'] agree. Add a test where codex rows are saturated but healthy and fallback stays False.

State that choice_key and the imminent blocker use effective free = min(row free, claude_rows) for claude rows, and add a test for a claude row with a large row free and a shared counter of 1 alongside a codex row.
Add concurrency.py to the trace list, or add a test that select_limit does not change for codex-only snapshots and does not double count for claude rows.
Add a test for saturated-but-healthy codex rows: fallback False, and admit defers with reason executor_capacity.
